The Villa · Costa Paradiso, Sardinia

Architectural Features of the Villa

The villa occupies one of the finest vantage points in Costa Paradiso. Its architecture, terraces and garden are shaped by the site itself — the granite coastline, the open sea, and the quiet rhythm of a Mediterranean hillside.

Panoramic Setting

A Panoramic Position

The villa occupies one of the finest vantage points in Costa Paradiso. From its generous terraces, panoramic views open across the Mediterranean Sea, the granite coastline and the Strait of Bonifacio. On clear days, the silhouette of Corsica is visible on the horizon, while in the opposite direction the island of Asinara — part of the national park bearing its name — can be seen in the distance.

In the evening, the villa becomes an ideal viewpoint for watching Sardinia's celebrated sunsets, as the sun sinks directly into the sea, tinting the granite cliffs and the water in shades of gold and rose.

Architecture

Architectural Character

The facades follow the tradition of Mediterranean modernism. Natural Sardinian granite, white plastered surfaces, timber shutters and restrained architectural forms come together in a coherent composition, set naturally within the surrounding rocky landscape.

Outdoor Living

Terraces and Garden

The generous terraces form a natural extension of the interior spaces, uniting the architecture with the open air. Mediterranean planting, ornamental shrubs, flowering species and natural stone shape the atmosphere of a secluded garden — characteristic of the finest coastal villas of northern Sardinia.

Seclusion

Privacy and Atmosphere

Distance from any town centre, the surrounding quiet, clean sea air and the immediate proximity of the coastline create exceptional conditions for rest. The architecture of the house is oriented toward an unhurried Mediterranean way of life, in which the true luxury lies in the harmony of nature, architecture and interior space.
